observation: Four refinement critique rounds did not repeat a defect: each round closed its predecessor's defect class and exposed a deeper one at the same seam — what population is being measured. R1: reach lists authored then justified in prose. R2: the derivation ran per module, so a symbol relocated across a package boundary contributed zero consumers and the audit was blind to a real importer. R3: the derivation population was fixed at files OUTSIDE framework/shared, so the package's own internal imports — which become cross-package crossings on split day — were never in it. R4: the founder's ruling read literally would have opened three zero-audience db:* surfaces. Every round's finding was load-bearing for a red build, not stylistic.
evidence: refine-critique.md:7-95 (rounds 1-3 recorded verbatim); founder-rulings.md:38-50 (round-4 predicate scoping); progress.json:19-41

observation: Each critique round re-measured the live tree at 0791c4fd rather than reading the artifact's numbers, and round 3 independently reproduced the full measured core to the number — 640 exported names with zero declared twice, 95 modules placed exactly once, the 382+336+8=726 import-site decomposition, 30 consumer packages / 31 manifests / 28 tsconfigs / 16 eslint refs, and all 18 production reach lists including the run-orchestration entry only a symbol-level pass finds. Independent reproduction is what made the standing blockers credible as decisions rather than opinions.

The reach-list derivation initially used the MODULE as its unit. A symbol relocated across a package boundary (ReturnEnforcementChannel) therefore contributed zero consumers to the audit, and the audit could not see its own error — harness-capability's reach omitted run-orchestration. Rebuilding the derivation with the exported NAME as the unit (640 names -> destination) also found a fifth flipping re-export site the reviewer's own pass had missed. The same choice later paid again at build time: the codemod moved 768 external sites by name, and seven substrate names collide with exports elsewhere in the repo, so a module-driven rewrite would have resolved e.g. Thread onto the database package and still compiled.
evidence: refine-critique.md:20-32; commit 3f95d2a0 body ('moved by name, not by module: seven of the substrate's names collide with exports elsewhere in the repo, so resolving Thread from memory lands on the database package and compiles')

observation: The derivation population excluded the package's own internal imports, so nine framework->framework edges that only exist AFTER the split (event-bus -> diagnostics, harness-protocol -> event-bus, tool-protocol -> harness-protocol, conversation-parts -> harness-capability, ...) were invisible until round 3. Each would have been forbidden by reach-declared-surfaces-only plus a second forbidden manifest crossing, so the new packages could not even have declared one another as dependencies. No precedent existed: not one of the model's 10 existing surfaces grants the framework role. A blast-radius class that only comes into existence at the moment of the change was not in the measured population.

The founder's ruling ('framework to framework imports should be fine') was recorded verbatim and then SCOPED by the orchestrator with the scoping written down as a separate, reversible, flagged decision: the literal text also admits db:schema-ns, db:unknown and db:testing — the whole-schema door and the undecided-surface catch-all — which would have granted all eighteen new packages production reach to a boundary a different work package (AU30/AU31) owns. The clause shipped admitting a framework source only when the target label is framework/<name>. Also flagged-not-actioned: the general ruling relaxes framework/design-system's written 'exactly one user interface' reason.
evidence: founder-rulings.md:29-50; commit 02a197db body; plan.md:40 (AU30/AU31 out of scope)

observation: Twice, one level apart, an artifact asserted that the attack harness's coverage property forced a break-test, and both times it forced nothing. P4: the claim was made for a CLAUSE change — coverageGaps keys entirely on REGISTERED RULE IDS, and reach-declared-surfaces-only is a clause id. P7: the same claim one level down for a CHECK added to an existing rule — registries-honest already satisfies coverageGaps via unowned-new-table, so adding a check to it forces nothing. Recorded as R7 'pattern, not incident'. Separately confirmed: property 2 (the control twin) is prose at governance-attacks.ts:20-21 that nothing evaluates. The mechanism reads stronger than it is.

Both false-enforcement claims were closed by moving the guarantee onto something that actually fails a build, not by restating it. For the clause: three forbidden decided-rules.json rows (db:schema-ns, db:unknown forbidden in both worlds; db:testing forbidden in production, allowed in development) gated by the frozen governance-model.test.ts reproduction loop — broaden the clause and all three go red. For AC-2's check: ship it as a NEW registered rule (framework-surfaces-declared) so property 4 bites on its positive case, explicitly instead of folding it into registries-honest. The residual — control twins remain convention-backed — is stated plainly rather than claimed.

Three architecture critique rounds, each finding a different structural class rather than detail. R1 (7 blocking): decisions and a red lint gate sat INSIDE the window where nothing typechecks. R2 (5 blocking): two whole rewrite classes fell outside the codemod's node shape — relative imports inside the package (239 production statements, 47 crossing a destination, plus 115 more in development files, 27 resolving to a dissolving barrel) and 45 import('@hyperidle/shared') sites (29 type positions, 16 runtime calls); a relative specifier is never @hyperidle/shared-shaped, so both the codemod AND the residual-grep check were structurally blind to all of them. R3 (3 blocking): development-file placement was enumerated wrong in BOTH directions, and the dependency block (dependencies vs devDependencies) silently decides which world a manifest crossing is judged in — a decision no artifact had made, and one that would have emitted eight forbidden production manifest crossings.

The architecture opened with an explicit invariant — 'the atomic window contains no judgement; every decision lands in Phase A, where a wrong one is a revert' — and discharged it by writing the Phase B inputs as artifacts the atomic commit merely consumes: the src-relative layout convention, the post-fold 80-module destination map, the floor baseline table, and an 86-row development-file placement with a computed subject rule. This made a no-shim, no-deprecation, every-package-touched change tractable as ten independently green and reversible preparation commits plus one atomic commit.
evidence: architecture.md:15-22 (R-A); phase-b-inputs.md; development-file-placement.md; place-development-files.ts; feasibility.md:385-409 ('The one-PR question'); git log 02a197db..3f95d2a0 (11 Phase-A commits)

observation: The in-package layout decision was made for a mechanical reason, not a stylistic one, and its cost was stated: keeping every module's path relative to src/ makes every SAME-package relative import byte-identical after the move, collapsing the codemod's second-pass population from 239 statements to 47. The accepted cost — redundant directory segments like block-derivation/src/blocks/ and harness-protocol/src/harness/ — is written down rather than discovered later.

A silent-failure class nearly shipped green: vi.mock takes its specifier as an ARGUMENT, not as an import, so the codemod never saw it — and a relative vi.mock of a path that no longer resolves is silently a no-op in vitest. The event bus logged for real and only one assertion (that handler exceptions are observable) noticed. verify runs no tests, so nothing in the verify chain could have caught it; it was found solely because a test lane was run and went red. Captured as an @lore comment at the site.
evidence: commit 872bfd19 body and its @lore in framework/event-bus/src/__tests__/event-bus.test.ts; CLAUDE.md verify table (verify runs no tests)

observation: The build proved each new mechanism red before green and did not settle for one break-test where the discriminating one was a pair. framework-surfaces-declared shipped with break-tests in both directions (package with no surfaces entry -> reported at its manifest; declared framework/<name> with no package behind it -> reported at the registry) and with a floor scoped to the framework subset so a scan finding no framework packages is a build error rather than a clean run. The Ruling-1 widening shipped with five cases including two control twins (framework reaching db:schema-ns and db:unknown must still be refused) — the two that tell the scoped reading from the literal one on the live tree. The audience-naming message shipped with a positive/negative pair so it tests the AUDIENCE and not the package name.
evidence: commits 7cbeb1f8, 5b7ab401, 3d7db7b1 (bodies); progress.json verdicts[0].evidence ('both new gates shown to bite AND shown to go red when disabled')

observation: The plan's own enumerations undercounted at least four times, each corrected inside a Phase-A commit rather than by re-planning: the adapter-pool re-export removal broke six same-package tests rather than being free; the scope-label republication had four readers, not one; the destination map held 80 production modules where requirements.md §4.9 said 79 (a module split had already happened); and the development-file enumeration found two more constructs with no successor that the enumeration discovered rather than predicted. Separately, both files an earlier architecture draft named as spanning multiple destinations were wrong, and 17 unnamed ones were real.

observation: AC-5 ('no module survives that nothing outside its own package reaches') had been reinterpreted by requirements.md §5.1 as co-location — reading 'package' as 'module'. The reinterpretation was surfaced to the founder rather than absorbed, and the literal reading was restored by ruling: nine modules folded into their real consumers and one deleted, computed to a fixpoint including modules the folding itself created. The ruling also disposed of the artifact's claim that AC-5 collided with the no-behaviour-change constraint — folding moves declarations between files and changes no function.

The work package's own artifacts carried inaccuracies that later phases had to correct. During the build, governance/README.md was found to state 124 decided rows against a live 118, and the governance-model fixture was found to invent a role for every package name it did not know — so a named row was decided by whichever clause caught it first. Review returned DONE with ten non-blocking findings, three of which were inaccuracies in artifacts AU34 itself delivered. Artifacts that state counts go stale against the tree they describe even within a single work package.
evidence: commit f0d558ca body ('The README stated 124 rows against a live 118'); progress.json verdicts[0] (nonBlocking: 10)

observation: Cost signals: sized L (~4d) in plan.md; ran in a single day, 03:10 -> 14:04 (~11h wall clock), 22 commits. Rework/decision rounds: 4 refinement critique rounds (6 + 2 + 4 + 1 blocking) and 3 architecture rounds (7 + 5 + 3 blocking) = 28 blocking findings before any code; 3 founder rulings. Build split 11 Phase-A preparation commits + 1 atomic commit (917 files) + 5 follow-ups. Final diff 1008 files, +9892 / -3860. Four of the 22 commits are pure planning artifacts. The large majority of the effort went to deciding and mechanizing WHAT could be measured and enforced, not to the move itself — which is the proportionality question this shape raises.
